title: Father and God of All Mankind
description: Father and God of All Mankind in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 29, “"Thy Kingdom Come."”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Fa-ther and God of all man-kind, And all the hosts a-bove, Let ev-ery un-der-stand-ing mind U-nite to praise Thy love.

lines: Father and God of all mankind,
Thy kingdom come, with power and grace,
Thy peace, and joy, and righteousness,
But makes an end of sin;
The joy that human thought transcends,
Now to our souls bring in:

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
